written_html:
Chemical manufacturing assets

Buy used chemical plants and equipment from International Process Plants (IPP)

International Process Plants (IPP) is the world’s largest seller of used process plants and equipment, with 15,000+ pieces of inventory and nearly five decades of experience. Our extensive stock of chemical process equipment includes reactors, heat exchangers, dryers, centrifuges, tanks, filters and complete plant lines, sourced from decommissioned, idled and restructured sites worldwide.

With operations in 15 countries and 20 complete process plant sites under ownership, we help chemical manufacturers of all sizes reduce capital risk, avoid long lead times and ramp up production capacity fast.

Company-wide figures published by IPP, checked October 7, 2026. Company profile and scale: SOCMA.

written_html:
From your brief to your site

How buying from IPP works

Bring your engineering requirements. IPP helps you establish the asset and service scope.

  1. Share your requirements

    Send the process, required capacity, materials of construction, operating conditions, destination and target timing. Include any stock numbers you have selected.

  2. Review specifications and inspect

    Request available photographs, drawings and equipment records. Arrange a video or on-site inspection with the IPP team.

  3. Agree the purchase scope

    Confirm the equipment included, commercial terms and services required. Ask about financing, which IPP advertises for its plants and equipment.

  4. Plan dismantling and relocation

    Coordinate teardown, loading and relocation requirements for the selected plant or system. Establish responsibilities and schedules before removal begins.

  5. Arrange shipping and start-up support

    IPP offers international shipping options, or buyers can arrange their own shipping. Discuss destination-site installation and start-up support as part of the project scope.

Services vary by asset and agreed scope. More about buying from IPP.

written_html:
Your questions, answered

FAQs

Discuss a specific stock number, plant package or surplus asset with IPP.

Ask an expert ↗
Does IPP offer full chemical plants for sale?

Yes. In addition to individual equipment, we sell complete chemical process plants, including teardown and relocation services.

Can I inspect the equipment before buying?

Yes. IPP offers on-site and video inspections for most equipment. Contact us to schedule one.

Where does IPP source its chemical equipment?

From multinational chemical producers, toll manufacturers and decommissioned or restructured facilities worldwide.

What is chemical process plant equipment?

This refers to the machines and systems used in chemical manufacturing, including reactors, exchangers, centrifuges, dryers, and more. Read our chemical process plant equipment guide.

How do I get a price for a chemical plant or equipment?

Contact IPP with the stock number or your process requirements. The quotation needs to define the assets included and any dismantling, loading, shipping or other services requested.

Can IPP help with international shipping?

Yes. IPP offers international shipping options, or buyers can arrange their own shipping. Confirm the asset’s location, loading requirements and delivery destination when discussing the purchase.

What documentation is available for a used plant?

Available documentation varies by asset. Ask IPP for equipment lists, drawings, process descriptions and inspection records for the plant or stock number you are considering.

Is financing available?

Yes. IPP advertises financing for its plants and equipment. Contact IPP to discuss availability and terms for your proposed purchase.

Does IPP buy shutdown chemical plants and surplus equipment?

Yes. IPP buys complete plants, process lines and individual equipment. Use the sell a plant or sell equipment form to start an assessment.

What information should I provide when selling?

Share an asset list, photographs, the plant location, available technical documents and your removal timeline. IPP’s team can then discuss the assessment and next steps.

How quickly can IPP assess assets for sale?

Send IPP your asset information and removal deadline to request a project-specific schedule. The team will need to establish the asset scope, available documentation and site access.

What happens to a chemical plant site after a sale?

A transaction may cover equipment for removal or an entire site. IPP’s published projects include equipment relocation and site repurposing. The purchase agreement defines which assets or property are included and who is responsible for the work.
